dish: the modern-classic tasting menu with French, Mediterranean and Japanese accents
w: Saarbrücken's two-MICHELIN-star flagship in the Nauwieser Viertel, in an 1890 Gründerzeit former school turned boutique hotel. Chef Silio Del Fabro — Gusto's Koch des Jahres 2026 — cooks supremely fresh, farm-sourced seasonal produce; the city's benchmark fine-dining table right in its creative quarter.

dish: original Wiener Schnitzel vom Kalbsrücken and the seasonal Menü Kunz
w: A century-old family restaurant-and-butcher in the village of Bliesen that has held a MICHELIN star for over two decades under Alexander and Anke Kunz. Precise French classics sit beside the house's own charcuterie and a famous Wiener Schnitzel — the Saarland's rural fine-dining destination and a Jeunes Restaurateurs member.

dish: the four/five-course seasonal market menu eaten at the counter
w: A tiny gastro-jewel in a Nauwieser-Viertel sandstone house (the birthplace of director Max Ophüls), run by ex-two-star chef Jens Jacob. Counter seats — 'le comptoir' — are the prize; evenings bring a modern four/five-course seasonal market menu. A MICHELIN-Guide selection.

dish: the weekly-changing three/four-course menu (with a vegetarian menu)
w: The relaxed counterpart to Esplanade in the same boutique-hotel building, taking over the fine-dining rooms when the two-star is dark. Modern cooking in weekly-changing three- or four-course menus, one of them vegetarian — a MICHELIN-Guide address at an accessible price.

dish: confit chicken with scalloped potatoes and fjord-trout with potato foam
w: A French bistronomie address in a well-kept townhouse just outside the centre, carrying a MICHELIN Bib Gourmand for good-value cooking — confit chicken with scalloped potatoes, fjord trout with potato foam. Reopened in spring 2026 under new owners Josianne Lerner and Paul Stiel, with a lovely front terrace.

dish: Hoorische and Gefillde (potato dumplings) with Speck sauce
w: A 25-year fixture on the St. Johanner Markt built entirely around the Saarland's potato canon — Hoorische, Gefillde, Geheirade and Dibbelabbes in a rustic room. The place to eat the region's home kitchen right in the old-town square.

dish: grilled Bratwurst and cold draught beer in the Saar-meadow beer garden
w: Saarbrücken's beloved riverside beer garden on the Staden meadows beside the Saar — bratwurst off the grill, sandwiches and cool draught beer under the trees, with a playground next door. A relaxed local favourite for young and old alike.

dish: Judd mat Gaardebounen with the house-brewed Clausel beer
w: One of the capital's oldest typical Luxembourgish tables, in the former Mousel brewery buildings in Clausen for some two centuries. Hearty local cooking — Judd mat Gaardebounen, choucroute garnie — washed down with the Clausel beer still brewed on the old brewery site.

dish: Judd mat Gaardebounen and seasonal Luxembourgish plates
w: A classic of the genre on the wooded edge of the Bambësch above Rollingergrund — a big hotel-restaurant with a huge terrace where Luxembourgish cooking is done simply but with care. A family standby for the national dish, name-checked by both ELLE and Paperjam.

dish: Judd mat Gaardebounen with bacon apples, and seasonal game
address: 400 Rue des Sept Arpents, 1149 Luxembourg, Luxembourg
w: A former 1873 hunting lodge in the heart of the Bambësch forest, reached on a woodland walk, serving revisited Luxembourgish cooking — Judd mat Gaardebounen with bacon apples, vol-au-vent, game in season — with a donkey pasture next door for the kids. A local favourite listed by ELLE and Paperjam.

dish: hearty Luxembourgish plates with Bofferding and Battin beers brewed on site
w: The convivial brewery brasserie inside the Brasserie Nationale in Bascharage, where Bofferding and Battin are brewed — wooden tables, malt in the air, French-Luxembourgish plates and, of course, the freshest possible beer. Recommended by ELLE and Visit Luxembourg.

dish: Quetschentaart (plum tart) and the house pralines and ice creams
w: A confectionery-pâtisserie institution since 1863, now in its sixth family generation and a Fournisseur de la Cour (royal warrant). Keeper of Luxembourg's sweet tradition — the autumn Quetschentaart — alongside chocolates, glaces and a fine-food counter in the Ville-Haute.

dish: the emblematic Bamkuch (Luxembourg tree cake)
w: A pâtisserie-traiteur house on the Grand-Rue, a Fournisseur de la Cour celebrating Luxembourg gastronomy for over 60 years. Its signature is the Bamkuch — the soft, faintly caramelised Luxembourg 'tree cake' — beside fine pastries and savoury delicacies.

dish: Luxembourg-style grilled pork knuckle with the house unfiltered beer
w: Luxembourg's only micro-brewery, in the 500-year-old former Mousel brewery at the Rives de Clausen — original steam engines and vats among the tables, unfiltered house beer, and traditional Luxembourgish plates (the grilled pork knuckle is the pick). A Bavarian-style brewpub for families by day and young revellers by night.

dish: classic cuisine with Luxembourg Moselle Riesling and Crémant over the valley
w: An elegant, classical restaurant on the heights above Remich commanding a sweeping view over the Luxembourg Moselle — the place to pair refined cooking with the valley's own Riesling, Pinot Gris and Crémant de Luxembourg. A MICHELIN-Guide address in the heart of the wine country.

dish: house-cured charcuterie and the classic Lorraine tasting menu
w: Sarreguemines' MICHELIN-starred table, a champion of tradition where the chef works with local market gardeners and buys whole animals to cure his own charcuterie. Classic, produce-driven cooking a stone's throw from the German border — the faience town's fine-dining benchmark.

dish: sandre au vin gris de Toul and kougelhopf perdu flambé à la mirabelle
w: Metz's grand Art Deco brasserie by the station — high ceilings, purple banquettes, wood panelling — long known as 'Le Flo'. Lorraine and Alsatian specialities carry the menu: potato terrine with Munster, pike-perch in Toul grey wine, and kougelhopf French-toast flambéed with mirabelle. A local institution listed by Inspire Metz and Lorraine Tourisme.

dish: quiche lorraine and tasting boards of Vosges smoked charcuterie at the covered market
address: Marché Couvert, Place de la Cathédrale, 57000 Metz, France
w: A Metz institution inside the historic covered market — Mauricette's stall of Grand Est produce (cheeses, Vosges smoked charcuterie, made-to-measure boards) plus the 'L'assiette du Marché' where you sit down to quiche lorraine, tourte, potée and flammekueche. No visit to the market is complete without a stop here.

dish: tarte aux mirabelles (Saturdays) and the chiboust mirabelle
address: 31 Rue de la Tête d'Or, 57000 Metz, France
w: A refined pâtisserie-chocolaterie-salon de thé in central Metz, keeper of the Lorraine sweet canon — its Saturday-only tarte aux mirabelles, the chiboust mirabelle, palets messins and Belles de Lorraine. Critic Gilles Pudlowski calls it 'really the best patisserie in Metz'.

dish: the estate-driven gourmet menu with own-vineyard Mosel Riesling
w: A MICHELIN-starred gourmet restaurant with boutique hotel and working winery in the wine village of Olewig, ringed by vineyards. Chef-vintner Wolfgang Becker pairs precise, creative cooking with Riesling from the family's own slate slopes — Trier's benchmark fine table (a simpler Becker's Weinhaus sits alongside).

dish: Roman dishes after Apicius (Lucanian sausages, wine rolls) with Mosel wine
w: A traditional Trier restaurant on the Hauptmarkt, unique for its Roman menu cooked from the ancient cookbook 'De re coquinaria' of Apicius — Lucanian sausages, wine rolls, lamb in fig sauce — served alongside regional dishes in a Roman wine cellar. Recently relaunched under new stewardship.

dish: Middle-Mosel Riesling from the estate in the 1416 crooked house
w: A tiny, top-heavy half-timbered wine tavern of 1416 on Bernkastel's market square, pouring more than 50 Rieslings and reds from its own cultivation. One of the Middle Mosel's most characterful spots for a glass of cool slate-slope Riesling.

dish: Trierer Rahmfleisch and filled potato dumplings
w: A cosy, long-popular Trier restaurant in the pedestrian zone built around the potato in every form — homemade potato bread and soups, baked potatoes, dumplings — plus regional plates like Trierer Rahmfleisch and filled potato dumplings. Generous, good-value 'Omas Küche' in the heart of the old town.
